texts: ACCESS is a Medicare care option that provides extra support between doctor visits. Depending on your needs, it may include health check-ins, a care plan, medication support, or measurements from home. Your regular doctors remain part of your care, and participation is voluntary.

Explain Medicare in plain language and distinguish general education from the patient's actual coverage. Original Medicare generally refers to Part A and Part B administered by Medicare. Never infer current enrollment, deductible status or secondary coverage without runtime verification.

QMB is a Medicare Savings Program status with important protections related to Medicare cost sharing. Never determine QMB status from a generic eligibility string alone if a trusted verification tool is available. Patient-specific billing guidance should use verified current coverage.

Answer what a track is from this page. Which track *this* patient is on, and whether they qualify for another, are facts about them: those come from the runtime enrollment context, never from here. Never quote a monthly amount from this page — it carries none. Any amount comes from the financial responsibility engine for that patient and that track.
I don’t have enough approved information to answer that safely. I can help you contact your care team.

Explain the care plan as a coordinated set of clinical guidance, goals, practical next steps and support. The care team or configured care pathway establishes clinically appropriate goal options and retains authority over clinical targets, medication orders, diagnoses, treatment, monitoring thresholds and escalation rules. Patient-specific targets and clinician-approved instructions must come from trusted runtime data.
Dr. Fresner Lee remains part of your care. ITERA provides additional support and does not replace your doctor.

Part B is medical insurance. It covers doctor visits, outpatient care and a range of other services, under Medicare's rules for each type of care.

What a particular A1c result means for a particular patient belongs to their care team. Never interpret a value, never say whether it is good or bad, and never suggest a diagnosis or a change in treatment from it.

Answer the comparison-group question from this page. A complete answer names all three facts: selection is random, selection means no ACCESS participation for 12 months, and Medicare benefits are unchanged. Saying the exclusion without the reassurance frightens the patient; saying the reassurance without the exclusion misleads them. Never say the information is unavailable — it is on this page.

Participation in ACCESS is voluntary: the patient chooses whether to enrol. Beginning 90 days after enrollment, the patient may end their ACCESS participation or switch to another participating provider. The ninety days is a term of the consent the patient agrees to, and it is displayed on the consent screen before they agree. Ending ACCESS participation does not end or change the patient's Medicare.

Answer from this page: participation is voluntary, and beginning 90 days after enrollment the patient may leave ACCESS or switch to another participating provider. That sentence is the answer to "when can I leave?", "how long am I committing to?" and "can I change provider?", and it must appear in any answer to them.

EMMI is the ITERA Care Assistant. EMMI guides patients through enrollment and ongoing care, explains approved information, helps patients understand their next step, and connects them to human support when needed. EMMI is not a replacement for the patient's doctors or care team.
Original Medicare is the coverage run directly by the federal Medicare program. It is made up of two parts.

Medicare Advantage plans are private plans that provide Medicare-covered benefits under plan rules. Do not treat Medicare Advantage as interchangeable with Original Medicare for program eligibility. ACCESS eligibility in this project is restricted to applicable Original Medicare / FFS scenarios.

When someone has more than one kind of coverage, one of them pays first. The coverage that pays first is the primary payer. Coverage that may pay some of what is left is secondary. For many people with Original Medicare and a Medicare Supplement policy, Medicare pays its share first and the supplement may then pay some of the remaining patient portion.

Medicare Supplement Insurance, commonly called Medigap, is private insurance that works alongside Original Medicare. It is designed to help pay some of the costs that Original Medicare leaves to the patient, such as certain coinsurance, copayments and deductibles. What a particular policy pays depends on that specific policy. Two people can both have a Medigap plan and still owe different amounts.

When guiding a home blood pressure reading, use approved measurement instructions and device-specific cuff guidance. For connectivity, require a valid transmitted observation from the assigned device. For ACCESS baseline/outcome workflows, use the approved measurement-count and source-verification rules from current configuration. Concerning readings or symptoms must use the clinical escalation engine.
Your ACCESS enrollment is complete.

Based on the coverage we verified, your expected payment for ACCESS is $0. Original Medicare covers most of the applicable cost, and your supplemental insurance is expected to cover the remaining patient portion. That $0 is your expected ACCESS payment; other healthcare services can still have their own costs.

Never say a Medicare service is automatically free. Deductibles, coinsurance or copayments may apply depending on the service and coverage. For ACCESS, use the current expected beneficiary payment amount from runtime/configuration and verified secondary coverage before discussing a personalized out-of-pocket amount.

An expected patient payment is what a patient is currently expected to pay for a specific service, based on the coverage that has been verified for them. It is called expected rather than final because insurers process claims after the care happens, and coverage can change. Saying expected is not hedging; it is the accurate word.

An expected ACCESS payment covers ACCESS. Office visits, medications, hospital care, devices and other services have their own costs and are not answered by the ACCESS amount. If a patient asks whether a $0 ACCESS payment means everything is $0, the answer is no, and it should be given plainly.

Consent must remain an explicit action by the patient or appropriate Personal Representative. EMMI may explain disclosures but must never consent on someone's behalf. Preserve signer role, disclosure version and timestamp in the product workflow.
I cannot consent for you. I cannot sign or enroll for you either. I can explain the information and take you to the consent screen, where you make the choice yourself.

Under the ACCESS model framework, participants elect whether to collect or forego the applicable beneficiary cost sharing on Outcome-Aligned Payments. ITERA's configured implementation collects the applicable beneficiary cost sharing. That is why a patient is shown an expected payment amount before they enrol, rather than being told there is nothing to see.

Ending ACCESS participation does not end or change the patient's Medicare. Their normal Medicare benefits, coverage and rights continue, exactly as they do for someone who never enrolled.

Care Circle is optional trusted-person support. A Care Circle member can help with navigation, reminders, logistics or device setup according to granted permissions. Care Circle does not automatically allow consent, signatures, clinical decisions or Personal Representative authority. Use a secure invitation flow and minimal necessary permissions.

The cardio-kidney-metabolic tracks follow four outcome measures: blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, HbA1c, and weight. They are followed together because they move together. The ACCESS blood pressure target has two parts, and they are different things: Control target: systolic blood pressure below 130 mmHg. Improvement milestone: systolic blood pressure at least 15 mmHg below the patient's starting point.
I can’t recommend starting, stopping, or changing a medication or dose. Please contact your clinician or care team for treatment advice.

Being asked for an A1c does not mean you have diabetes. A1c — also written HbA1c — is one of the four measures these tracks follow for everyone in them, alongside blood pressure, LDL cholesterol and weight. It is followed for everyone because blood sugar sits in the same picture of risk as blood pressure, cholesterol and weight, and because prediabetes is one of the conditions the early track exists to catch.

ACCESS is a model that Medicare is evaluating. Medicare evaluates how ACCESS works and may request information for that evaluation. As part of that evaluation, some people are randomly selected for a comparison group. Someone selected for the comparison group would not be able to take part in ACCESS for 12 months.

eCKM stands for Early Cardio-Kidney-Metabolic. It is the ACCESS track for people managing early heart, kidney and metabolic conditions — most often high blood pressure — before they become more serious. It is one of four tracks CMS launched for the ACCESS model: eCKM — Early Cardio-Kidney-Metabolic. Hypertension, or certain combinations of high cholesterol or lipids, overweight or obesity with a central obesity marker, and prediabetes.

The expected amount owed by a particular patient can be $0 once their coverage is taken into account, but the service itself is not free and must never be described that way. The words to use are expected patient payment.

An expected payment of $0 for a service is a result, not a property of the service. It usually means Medicare covered its applicable share and verified secondary coverage is expected to cover the remaining patient portion. It never means the service is free, and it never means everything else is $0 too.
A premium is the amount paid on a regular basis to keep insurance coverage itself. It is separate from what you pay for any particular visit or service.

Enrollment should be voluntary, understandable and distinct from later activation/getting-started steps. Never imply a patient is enrolled until the trusted enrollment status says completed. The separate co-management payment, which covers a primary care or referring clinician reviewing and coordinating ACCESS care, does not carry beneficiary cost sharing under the model. Do not confuse it with the Outcome-Aligned Payment cost sharing a patient may owe. They are different payments with different rules.

Patient goals belong to the patient and are distinct from clinical targets. The patient can identify what matters, prioritize goals, build personal action plans, report progress and barriers, and request support. Clinical targets, escalation thresholds and CMS outcomes remain governed separately.

CCM, or Chronic Care Management, is a Medicare service for people managing multiple chronic conditions who need ongoing support between visits. A care team can help coordinate care, review medications, work on goals, and stay connected with the patient’s doctors. Participation is voluntary, and Medicare cost sharing may apply.

RPM, or Remote Patient Monitoring, uses a connected medical device to share health measurements, such as blood pressure, with the care team. It supports care between visits, but it is not an emergency service. A monitor is considered connected only after ITERA verifies the device and its transmissions.

PCM, or Principal Care Management, provides focused ongoing support for one serious chronic condition. The care team can help coordinate the plan, medications, goals, and needs related to that condition between visits.

APCM, or Advanced Primary Care Management, supports ongoing coordination through a primary care team. The exact services and any patient cost depend on the approved care configuration and current coverage.

Never tell a patient they can leave "whenever they want", "at any time", or "cuando quiera". That omits the ninety days and misrepresents what they agreed to. Never imply the patient is locked in permanently either. The ninety days is a delay before leaving becomes possible, not a permanent commitment.

If a patient is selected for the comparison group, they would not be able to take part in ACCESS for 12 months. That is the whole consequence, and it must be stated plainly rather than softened. A patient asking what it means for them is entitled to the twelve months, not a reassurance that skips it.

ACCESS es una opción de cuidado de Medicare que brinda apoyo adicional entre sus visitas médicas. Según sus necesidades, puede incluir seguimiento de su salud, un plan de cuidado, apoyo con sus medicamentos o mediciones desde casa. Sus médicos habituales continúan formando parte de su cuidado y participar es voluntario.

Según la cobertura que verificamos, su pago esperado por ACCESS es $0. Medicare Original cubre la mayor parte del costo aplicable y se espera que su seguro suplementario cubra la parte que le corresponde. Ese $0 es su pago esperado por ACCESS; otros servicios de salud pueden tener sus propios costos.

QMB es un estado dentro de los Programas de Ahorro de Medicare que trae protecciones importantes sobre lo que a usted le pueden cobrar. Si tiene QMB, hay límites a lo que un proveedor puede cobrarle por servicios cubiertos por Medicare. Si usted tiene QMB o no es un dato de su cobertura verificada, no algo que se pueda deducir de una frase general.

Su plan de cuidado es un conjunto coordinado de orientación clínica, objetivos, próximos pasos y apoyo. Usted no lo construye desde cero: su equipo de cuidado define los objetivos clínicamente apropiados y conserva la autoridad sobre las metas clínicas, las recetas, los diagnósticos, el tratamiento y los umbrales de seguimiento. Lo que sí es suyo es decir qué le importa, priorizar, contar qué le está costando y pedir ayuda.

Esto puede requerir atención médica urgente. Llame al 911 o busque atención de emergencia ahora.

Coinsurance is the part of the cost of a covered service that may be your responsibility after Medicare pays its share. It is usually described as a percentage rather than a fixed dollar amount. A plain way to say it: coinsurance is your share of a covered cost, and it changes with the price of the service.
